world.paradise_isle.desc: A small crescent of green rock and white sand where the tide keeps the time, the reef feeds everyone, and a name is worth more than a boat.
paradise_isle.npc.1.desc: Your grandmother, who mends nets at the door and knows every reef by heart.
paradise_isle.npc.1.l1: The sea gives and the sea takes; we are only the ones who carry the net.
paradise_isle.npc.1.l2: Eat something, child—you are all bones and salt.
paradise_isle.npc.2.desc: A free-diver your age, first into the water and last out of it.
paradise_isle.npc.2.l1: Race you to the reef! Last one in guts the catch.
paradise_isle.npc.2.l2: The big ones always live past the break—I'll show you.
paradise_isle.npc.3.desc: The retired boatwright who can read a hull like a face.
paradise_isle.npc.3.l1: A boat will tell you when she is tired, if you listen to her ribs.
paradise_isle.npc.3.l2: I built her with my hands; I can read her the way you read the water.
paradise_isle.npc.4.desc: Keeper of the chapel of the tide, devout and quick to judge.
paradise_isle.npc.4.l1: The sea is not yours to buy and sell, whatever the trader tells you.
paradise_isle.npc.4.l2: You missed the festival again. The tide notices, even if you don't.
paradise_isle.npc.5.desc: The fish-market master, gruff as a barnacle and honest as a scale.
paradise_isle.npc.5.l1: Scales don't lie, and neither does a short weight. Count again.
paradise_isle.npc.5.l2: Bring me a catch like last week's and we'll talk about your own stall.
paradise_isle.npc.6.desc: Your little sister, all questions and salt-wet hair.
paradise_isle.npc.6.l1: Can I come on the boat tomorrow? I promise I'll sit still!
paradise_isle.npc.6.l2: Nan says you used to be scared of the water too.
paradise_isle.npc.7.desc: Who lost her husband to a squall and will not forgive your kin.
paradise_isle.npc.7.l1: Your family's luck is bought, and one day the sea will send the bill.
paradise_isle.npc.7.l2: Don't talk to me of grief—you have never lost anyone to a squall.
paradise_isle.npc.8.desc: Steady-handed and always smelling of tar and wood shavings.
paradise_isle.npc.8.l1: Bring her in at low tide and I'll see to her keel.
paradise_isle.npc.8.l2: Wood remembers. Treat her well and she'll outlive us both.
paradise_isle.npc.9.desc: Who has sailed every current and speaks mostly in proverbs.
paradise_isle.npc.9.l1: The current off the point will take a careless swimmer. Ask me how I know.
paradise_isle.npc.9.l2: I've sailed every water between here and the mainland, and the island is still the best of them.
paradise_isle.npc.10.desc: Whose voice calls the fleet home through the fog.
paradise_isle.npc.10.l1: When the fog comes, my voice is all the boats have to steer by.
paradise_isle.npc.10.l2: Sing with me at the festival—even a cracked voice counts.
paradise_isle.era.1.desc: The first islanders dragged their boats onto an empty shore and learned the tide's moods by losing nets to them.
paradise_isle.era.2.desc: The reef fed everyone; the storehouses were full and the weddings went on for a week.
paradise_isle.era.3.desc: A summer that would not end; the reef bleached, and the water drew back from the wells.
paradise_isle.era.4.desc: The winds died for a whole season; the boats sat idle and people learned to quarrel with their neighbours.
paradise_isle.era.5.desc: The great schools came back; the island worked the nets all night and forgave its old quarrels.
paradise_isle.era.6.desc: The island found its footing again, and people say the light on the evening water has never been finer.
paradise_isle.fac.1.desc: Those who work the nets and lines; the island eats because they row out before dawn.
paradise_isle.fac.2.desc: The chapel of the tide and its keepers; they guard the old rites and the lamp on the point.
paradise_isle.fac.3.desc: The family that bends every hull on the island, and holds the guild's rule on who may repair one.
paradise_isle.fac.4.desc: The council that sets the fishing laws and divides the common land.
paradise_isle.fac.5.desc: The singers whose voices call the fleet home through fog, and who keep the island's memory in song.
paradise_isle.reg.1.desc: A shallow crescent of white sand where the boats are hauled up and the children learn to swim.
paradise_isle.reg.2.desc: Thatch and coral-stone under the palms, with the well at its centre and every door known to you.
paradise_isle.reg.3.desc: The great reef that shelters the bay, bright with fish and dangerous at the turn of the tide.
paradise_isle.reg.4.desc: The long timber jetty where the catch is landed and the market begins.
paradise_isle.reg.5.desc: Slabs, scales, and shouting; the island's coin and its gossip change hands together.
paradise_isle.reg.6.desc: The tower on the headland where a watcher counts the sails on the horizon.
paradise_isle.reg.7.desc: The lamp on the point that burns through every storm to bring the boats home.
paradise_isle.lore.1.body: The first islanders came in three boats and lost two of them to the reef. They named the island Paradise because they had survived, and because no one argued.
paradise_isle.lore.2.body: The reef gives, but it keeps the right to take back. Every family has a name it speaks aloud only when the moon tide is running high.
paradise_isle.lore.3.body: The common land belongs to no one and feeds everyone. The Elders may divide its fruit but may never sell its soil.
paradise_isle.lore.4.body: Spring, neap, and the moon tide. The old ones say a life is measured by how well you keep your footing through all three.
paradise_isle.lore.5.body: Ambition is a heavy net, the old fishers say: it brings up the whole catch, or it drags you over the side with it.
paradise_isle.lore.6.body: A true teacher does not show you where the fish are; he teaches you to read the water and lets you find them yourself.
paradise_isle.lore.7.body: On this island a door is never barred. If you are hungry, you knock; if you are ashamed to knock, someone knocks for you.
paradise_isle.lore.8.body: Some young fishers leave for the mainland's money. The old ones do not stop them, only ask that they come back for the weddings.
paradise_isle.lore.9.body: Every islander who crosses to the mainland learns that salt water tastes the same everywhere, and the taste of home does not.
paradise_isle.lore.10: The Long Memory of the Jetty
paradise_isle.lore.10.body: At sixty an islander understands: the jetty remembers every boat that ever left it, and waits for all of them.
paradise_isle.lore.11.body: In the chapel hangs a small boat, half-built, with no name on it. Whose it was, and why it was never finished, no one living will say.
paradise_isle.lore.12: The Diver Who Went Too Deep
paradise_isle.lore.12.body: The deeper the dive, the slower the surfacing. The best divers on the island are the ones who learned to wait.
paradise_isle.lore.13.body: Before you take a boat of your own you must write a list: who you owe, who owes you, and what you will do when the storm comes.
paradise_isle.lore.14.body: At forty-five a fisher's hardest season is the calm: too much time to think about the boats that never came home.
paradise_isle.lore.15.body: Someone carried your catch to market as their own, and so you ate that winter. The hand that feeds you is not always yours.
paradise_isle.lore.16.body: On the night of the great storm the reef was said to sing, and every boat that heard it turned for home in time. The ones that did not are still out there.
paradise_isle.fate.1.desc: You will hold the island's nets and its secrets, and never fish far enough to be free of either.
paradise_isle.fate.2.desc: You will grow rich enough to buy a fleet, and never buy back a morning on the water.
paradise_isle.fate.3.desc: You will go deeper than is wise, and bring back a beauty no one on shore can name.
paradise_isle.fate.4.desc: Your voice will belong not to you but to the fog, and to every boat it brings safely home.
paradise_isle.fate.5.desc: You will build boats for other people's journeys, and your own will always be the one still on the stocks.
paradise_isle.fate.6.desc: You will outlive the fleet, and be the one who teaches the last child to read the water.
paradise_isle.we.1: The Wedding of the Two Bays
paradise_isle.we.1.body: Two families long at odds are joined at the Palm Shore, and for one week the whole island forgets which bay it belongs to.
paradise_isle.we.2.body: The fish come back in numbers no one alive has seen; the nets cannot hold them all, and for a season the island eats like kings.
paradise_isle.we.3: The Storm That Took the Jetty
paradise_isle.we.3.body: A typhoon snaps the long jetty in two; rebuilding it takes a whole season, and binds the island tighter than any law could.
paradise_isle.we.4.body: The tide-singer loses her voice, and for a season the boats go out without a song to call them home.
paradise_isle.we.5.body: A company offers to buy the common land for a price that would make every family rich and the island no longer theirs.
paradise_isle.we.6.body: After the hard years the island finds its footing again, and the evening light on the water seems to promise it will last.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.1.text: A mainland pedlar unrolls a mat of cheap glass floats on the Shell Bay sand and swears they read the shallows better than any eye.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.1.listen.note: His floats are cracked, but his tale of the outer shoals is worth the morning.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.1.turn.note: He rolls up his mat and mutters about islanders who think the sea belongs to them.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.2.text: A sunburnt woman knocks at your door and says your late father promised her a boat the family never gave.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.2.listen.note: Her story has holes, yet your mother's name inside it leaves you uneasy.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.2.turn.note: You hear her tell the whole lane, and by evening the lane believes her.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.3.text: A pearl-diver surfaces empty-handed at the reef and offers to lead you to a wreck no one else can reach.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.3.listen.note: The chart is drawn on oilcloth in a steady hand, and the wreck sounds real.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.3.turn: Dive alone or not at all
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.3.turn.note: He shrugs, says the reef keeps its secrets, and vanishes under the swell.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.4.text: A trader waits at the jetty's end, offering coin for your whole night's catch before a single fish has landed.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.4.listen.note: The coin is good; the catch is sold before it ever leaves the water.
paradise_isle.ev.stranger.4.turn.note: He laughs at your stubbornness; by dawn the market is full and the prices are low.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.1.text: Someone has prised the copper from the lighthouse door and left the lamp unlit on a moonless night.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.1.chase.note: You catch a village boy with the copper under his shirt, weeping for his sick mother.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.1.yield.note: You trim the wick by hand and stand watch till dawn, saying nothing to anyone.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.2.text: In the morning crush a hand slips your best snapper off the slab and into a basket of greens.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.2.chase.note: You corner a fishwife who swears she paid your brother for it; your brother says nothing.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.2.yield.note: You count the loss in coins and let the thief become a story told at the well.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.3.text: Someone has been cutting living coral from the reef by night, and the shallows are bleaching where they worked.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.3.chase.note: You find two men from the next bay with sacks of coral; they flee at your shout.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.3.yield.note: The Elders promise to look into it, and the cutting goes on for another season.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.4.text: A crate of your dried fish vanishes from the Old Pier while you mend a net ten paces away.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.4.chase.note: You find the crate behind the boathouse, half-empty, and the Boatwright's son red-faced beside it.
paradise_isle.ev.theft.4.yield.note: You keep a spare crate hidden after that, and trust your neighbours a little less.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.1.text: A fever walks the village with the moon tide; by evening three households have hung a white shell on the door.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.1.nurse.note: You hold a child's hand through the worst night and catch the fever yourself.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.1.avoid.note: You sleep aboard and stay well, and the village notices that too.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.2.text: The market is hushed; the woman who guts fastest coughs into her sleeve and will not go home.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.2.nurse: Send her to bed and take her knife
paradise_isle.ev.illness.2.nurse.note: You gut fish till your hands cramp, and she recovers enough to scold you for it.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.2.avoid.note: You take your trade to the next stall; she never quite forgives you.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.3.text: Children play on the Palm Shore though the fever is in the village, and a mother begs you to watch them.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.3.nurse.note: You keep them cool and fed till the fever passes over their house.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.3.avoid.note: She finds another watcher; one child falls ill, and you hear of it.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.4.text: The old watchman at the Lookout burns with fever but will not leave his post.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.4.nurse.note: You climb the tower each dusk for a week and learn every light on the horizon.
paradise_isle.ev.illness.4.avoid.note: They send a boy who sleeps through the night; no harm comes, and it rankles still.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.1.text: A bottle washes up at Shell Bay with a foreign coin sealed inside and a name you do not know.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.1.invest.note: The new net pays for itself by the third haul.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.1.save.note: You set the coin on the shelf and sleep soundly on it.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.2.text: The mainland boat overpaid for last season's dried fish and no one has come to reclaim the difference.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.2.invest.note: Your gear is the talk of the market, and your catch proves it.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.2.save.note: You tuck the coins away and let the season decide.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.3.text: A diver finds a purse of old coins in the reef's blue cave and shares it with whoever helped carry the catch.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.3.invest: Buy a share in a boat
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.3.invest.note: The boat turns a profit, and your name goes on her papers.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.3.save.note: You bury the coins in the boathouse and forget exactly where.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.4.text: The annual boat-race prize is doubled this year, and your crew has the fastest hull on the island.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.4.invest.note: You win by a length, and the winnings buy a month of calm.
paradise_isle.ev.windfall.4.save.note: You win the cup and keep your coin, and the crowd loves you for it.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.1.text: The friend who keeps the lighthouse lamp with you has been selling the oil and filling the reservoir with seawater.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.1.confront.not: He weeps, and you light the lamp yourself that night; the friendship ends there.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.1.plan.note: You note each shorted measure and wait for the chance to name it aloud.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.2: A Trusted Hand · the Fish Market
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.2.text: Your oldest partner has been weighing the catch with a stone in the scale, and the market trusts him, not you.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.2.confront.not: The market turns on you for the shouting, and he smiles behind his hand.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.2.plan: Beat him at his own scale
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.2.plan.note: You buy your own true scale and quietly outsell him all season.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.3.text: A diver you trained has been showing your secret reef to outsiders for coin.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.3.confront.not: You find him guiding a mainland boat and cut the line; he never dives your reef again.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.3.plan.note: You let it be known the reef is fished out; the outsiders stop coming, and so does he.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.4: A Trusted Hand · the Old Pier
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.4.text: Your brother has been taking your boat out by night without asking and bringing her home dirty.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.4.confront: Wait at the pier for him
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.4.confront.not: He admits it, and for a while he asks first; then he leaves the island.
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.4.plan: Put a lock on the oars
paradise_isle.ev.betrayal.4.plan.note: He climbs in over the stern, laughing; nothing changes.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.1.text: The chapel holds its tide-festival, and a place on the chanting bench waits empty at your side.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.1.join.note: The old hymns rise with the smoke, and your voice is steady for once.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.1.work.note: The chapel fills and empties; you finish three nets and feel the day pass over you.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.2.text: The market closes at noon for the catch-feast, and the long tables groan with grilled snapper.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.2.join.note: You eat till you cannot move and hear the best lie of the year.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.2.work.note: You balance the ledgers while the smell of grilled fish drifts in from the shore.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.3.text: The young people light fires along the Palm Shore to welcome the long summer.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.3.join.note: You dance until your feet ache and kiss someone under the palms.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.3.work.note: You watch the tide creep toward the hulls all night, and nothing burns.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.4.text: From the Lookout the whole island watches the Boatwright's daughter married, lanterns strung from mast to mast.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.4.join.note: You are pulled into the dancing and end the night hoarse with laughing.
paradise_isle.ev.festival.4.work.note: You tend the coals and hear the music from a distance, and are glad.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.1.text: They say at Shell Bay that you kept a boat from a drowning man to save your own nets.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.1.trace.note: You trace it to a cousin you refused a loan, and say so in the square.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.1.ignore.note: The story grows a little each telling, then is swallowed by a storm.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.2.text: The village whispers that your family's luck comes from a bargain struck with the sea.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.2.trace: Ask the Elders to end it
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.2.trace.note: An Elder speaks for you at the well, and the whispering stops, for now.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.2.ignore.note: Your laugh is taken for guilt, and the story gains a hook.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.3.text: Someone says you cut coral on the reef by night and sold it to a mainland trader.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.3.trace.note: You take three fishers to the untouched reef and let them see the lie themselves.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.3.ignore.note: The rumour keeps the market wary of you until the next big catch.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.4.text: On the jetty they say your last big haul was poached from another crew's nets.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.4.trace.note: It is the other crew's own boy, boasting; you make him say it aloud.
paradise_isle.ev.rumor.4.ignore.note: You fish hard and true, and the jetty slowly forgets.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.1.text: A trader's road leads north along the cliffs to a village none of you have ever seen.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.1.go.note: You trade shells for mainland salt and come home with stories.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.1.stay.note: You stay, and the road stays a line on the horizon.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.2.text: The mainland boat will take one passenger to the port where the big ships call.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.2.go.note: You stand on a foreign quay and feel the island shrink behind you.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.2.stay.note: The boat leaves without you; the harbour smells of tar and regret.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.3.text: A diver speaks of a reef across the deep that no islander has ever fished.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.3.go.note: The far reef is stranger and richer, and its current nearly takes you.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.3.stay.note: You keep to the known water and sleep well.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.4: The Open Road · the Long Jetty
paradise_isle.ev.journey.4.text: A whaling crew offers you a berth for a season on the far side of the world.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.4.go.note: You learn the cold southern stars and come home with a scar and a song.
paradise_isle.ev.journey.4.stay.note: You wave them off and keep your feet on island stone.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.1.text: A rival fisher challenges you to a contest of net-mending before the chapel, for the honour of the bench.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.1.fight.note: Your knots hold when his slip; the crowd cheers and he sulks.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.1.decline.note: You concede with a smile and he struts, and no one respects it.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.2.text: A rival bids against you for the best slab until the whole market turns to watch.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.2.fight.note: You take the snapper and the profit, and he remembers it.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.2.decline.note: He pays double for a fish going soft, and the stallholder winks at you.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.3.text: A young diver claims he can hold his breath longer than you, and the beach gathers round.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.3.fight.note: You surface first, lungs burning, and he claps you on the back.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.3.decline.note: You let him boast; the beach believes him, and you know better.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.4.text: A visiting sailor bets you cannot name every light on the horizon by dusk.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.4.fight.note: You name each one into the dark, and the sailor buys the drinks.
paradise_isle.ev.duel.4.decline.note: You admit it honestly; the sailor respects it, and buys the drinks anyway.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.1.text: The catch comes in heavy at Shell Bay and the Elders must decide who dries what before the flies get it.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.1.share.note: Every household gets a share, and the oldest are served first.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.1.hoard: Take the best for your own
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.1.hoard.note: Your rafters are heavy with fish and your name is light.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.2.text: The breadfruit and taro ripen at once, and the storehouse is too small for it all.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.2.share.note: Children carry breadfruit door to door, and the village smells of roasting.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.2.hoard: Sell the surplus to the trader
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.2.hoard.note: You fill your purse and watch the trader sail off with your neighbours' dinner.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.3.text: The reef yields a rare run of pearl-shell, and every diver's family wants a share of the deep pools.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.3.share.note: The shell is sold together and split evenly, and the quarrel dies.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.3.hoard.note: You take the richest shells, and the other divers see you do it.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.4.text: A great school drives into the bay and the whole island must work the nets through the night.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.4.share.note: By dawn the jetty is piled with silver, and not one boat goes home empty.
paradise_isle.ev.harvest.4.hoard.note: Your hold is fullest, and the other boats come in to a stripped bay.
paradise_isle.ev.law.1.text: The Elders decree that no one may fish within a rope's length of the reef until the new moon.
paradise_isle.ev.law.1.obey.note: You lose a week's catch and find the reef fatter the next season.
paradise_isle.ev.law.1.defy.note: You take a fine catch, and a fine from the Elders.
paradise_isle.ev.law.2.text: A new market rule sets a fixed price for snapper, whatever the sea gives.
paradise_isle.ev.law.2.obey.note: You take less coin, and the poor eat well that winter.
paradise_isle.ev.law.2.defy.note: You make good money until the market master catches you at it.
paradise_isle.ev.law.3.text: The chapel forbids cutting coral for ornament, on pain of shunning.
paradise_isle.ev.law.3.obey.note: Your hands stay clean and your trade takes the slow road.
paradise_isle.ev.law.3.defy.note: The trader pays well, and the chapel's silence follows you to the well.
paradise_isle.ev.law.4.text: The Boatwrights' guild rules that only its members may repair a hull on the island.
paradise_isle.ev.law.4.obey.note: You pay, and your boat is sound, and your purse is light.
paradise_isle.ev.law.4.defy.note: Your mend holds for a season, and the guild remembers your name.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.1.text: At the tide-festival a voice beside you in the chanting rises clear and steady, and you turn to look.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.1.woo.note: You walk the shore path slowly, and the walk takes all night.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.1.friend.not: You become the one she tells everything to, and nothing more.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.2.text: The fishwife's daughter laughs at your haggling and gives you the better fish for less.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.2.woo: Bring her a gift of shell
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.2.woo.note: She wears the shell on a cord, and the whole market teases you both.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.2.friend.not: You trade jokes across the slab for years and never say the word.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.3.text: A mainland girl staying with the chapel walks the Palm Shore alone at dusk.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.3.woo.note: You watch the sun go down together, and she misses her boat home.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.3.friend.not: She sails at dawn; you never learn her name.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.4.text: Under the Lookout's lantern you meet a diver from the next bay, salt in her hair and a laugh you cannot forget.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.4.woo.note: She stays a season, and the season is the best of your life.
paradise_isle.ev.first_love.4.friend.not: She sails home; you keep the shell she left and the shape of her laugh.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.1.text: The old net-mender of Shell Bay is found at peace in her chair, a half-mended net across her knees.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.1.mourn.note: You sit three nights with the family and learn who she really was.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.1.carry.note: You finish her net and use it every season, and think of her each haul.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.2.text: A child of the village is taken by the fever, and the whole lane falls silent.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.2.mourn.note: You do the hard work no one speaks of, and the mother holds your hand.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.2.carry.note: You row out alone and let the sea have your grief, and come back hollow.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.3.text: A diver does not surface at the reef, and the search goes on till the light fails.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.3.mourn.note: You find him in the blue cave and carry him up, and carry it ever after.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.3.carry.note: The reef never gives him back; you teach his son to dive in his place.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.4.text: Old Salt, who taught you the currents, dies on the pier with the tide coming in.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.4.mourn.note: The island drinks to him till dawn and tells his lies as if they were true.
paradise_isle.ev.grief.4.carry.note: You sail the old man's line one last time and leave his nets to the sea.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.1.text: The lighthouse keeper asks you to help trim the great lamp before the storm season.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.1.take.note: You learn which glass to polish and how the light must fall.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.1.refuse.note: You keep to your own work; the keeper finds another hand.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.2.text: The market master offers you a stall of your own if you can gut a hundred fish before noon.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.2.take.note: Your hands are a blur, and by noon the stall is yours.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.2.refuse: Stay a hand, not a master
paradise_isle.ev.craft.2.refuse.note: You keep your place and your steady wage, and no responsibility.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.3.text: An old diver offers to teach you the blue-cave breath, the trick that keeps a lung calm in the deep.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.3.take.note: You learn to go deeper and longer than you ever dared.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.3.refuse.note: You keep to water where you can see the bottom, and stay safe.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.4.text: The Boatwright needs a second pair of hands to bend a new hull before the wood dries.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.4.take.note: You learn the grain of wood in your palms.
paradise_isle.ev.craft.4.refuse.note: The hull is launched without your hands, and you wonder what you missed.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.1.text: In the chapel you find the tide-singer weeping over a letter from the mainland.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.1.open.note: She tells you she is leaving, and begs you tell no one till the boats sail.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.1.leave.note: You keep your distance, and learn of her leaving only when the chapel falls silent.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.2.text: You see the market master short-weighting a widow's purchase and pocketing the difference.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.2.open.note: The market turns on him, and the widow eats well that night.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.2.leave.note: You keep the knowledge, and the market master keeps his post.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.3.text: You find a diver cutting coral in the blue cave, against the chapel's law and the Elders' word.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.3.open.note: The Elders shun him for a season, and the reef is left to heal.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.3.leave.note: He stops, and thanks you, and owes you a debt he never names.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.4.text: On the pier at night you overhear two Elders planning to sell the common land to a mainland buyer.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.4.open.note: The village rises, and the sale dies, and the Elders mark your name.
paradise_isle.ev.secret.4.leave.note: The sale goes through; the common becomes a plantation, and you watch it happen.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.1.text: The rain has failed and the wells of Shell Bay are down to mud.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.1.ration.note: You count the water jars and drink last yourself.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.1.take.note: You fill your jars first, and the queue behind you says nothing, and remembers.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.2.text: The stream that feeds the village has shrunk to a trickle, and the Elders must decide who drinks.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.2.ration.note: You carry water to the old and carry none back for yourself.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.2.take.note: You stand over your well with a stick, and your family drinks.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.3.text: The lagoon has grown warm and salt, and the fish have gone deep.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.3.ration.note: You row past the reef each dawn and come back with just enough.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.3.take.note: You take the last of the shallows, and the lagoon stays empty for years.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.4.text: The mainland trader will sell water, but the price is cruel and the island's coin is low.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.4.ration.note: The one cask sees the village through, barely.
paradise_isle.ev.drought.4.take.note: You buy water for all, and owe the trader your boat.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.1.text: Someone has left a jar of honey at the lighthouse door with no name on it.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.1.accept.note: The honey is wild and dark, and you never learn whose it was.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.1.suspect.note: It sits until the ants find it, and you wonder all season.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.2: A Small Kindness · the Fish Market
paradise_isle.ev.gift.2.text: The stallholder slips an extra fish into your basket and refuses payment.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.2.accept.note: You give her your best shell in return, and the exchange becomes a habit.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.2.suspect.note: She shrugs and takes the fish back, and the stall is colder after.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.3.text: A diver you barely know leaves a perfect pearl on your boat's thwart.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.3.accept.note: You set the pearl in a ring and wear it every festival.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.3.suspect.note: You learn it was a boy from the next bay; by the time you thank him he has sailed.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.4: A Small Kindness · the Old Pier
paradise_isle.ev.gift.4.text: The widow who blames your family leaves fresh bread on your step in the hard season.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.4.accept.note: The bread is warm, and something cold between the houses thaws a little.
paradise_isle.ev.gift.4.suspect.note: You return the loaf untouched, and the silence between you hardens.
paradise_isle.ev.war.1.text: Raiders from a far island burn the fishing boats of the next bay, and the chapel calls the village to arms.
paradise_isle.ev.war.1.serve.note: You stand watch on the shore each night and learn how quickly courage runs out.
paradise_isle.ev.war.1.hide.note: You row the family to a hidden cove and wait out the raids.
paradise_isle.ev.war.2.text: The market empties; the mainland navy is pressing islanders into service.
paradise_isle.ev.war.2.serve.note: You serve a year on a foreign deck and come home older.
paradise_isle.ev.war.2.hide.note: You stay, and the navy takes your neighbour instead.
paradise_isle.ev.war.3.text: The Palm Shore becomes a landing beach; the Elders ask for volunteers to watch the shallows.
paradise_isle.ev.war.3.serve.note: You lie in the wet sand all night and see a sail that turns out to be driftwood.
paradise_isle.ev.war.3.hide.note: You sleep through the alarm and wake to news of a landing two bays over.
paradise_isle.ev.war.4.text: From the Lookout you see the raiders' sails before anyone else, and the village waits on your word.
paradise_isle.ev.war.4.serve.note: The fire flares, the village scatters, and the raiders find an empty bay.
paradise_isle.ev.war.4.hide.note: You keep the fire dark, and the raid comes down on the sleeping village.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.1.text: The nets come in empty three days running and the drying racks are bare.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.1.share.note: The village eats thin soup together and no one starves.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.1.close.note: Your children are full, and at night you hear another child crying.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.2.text: The trader's price for rice has tripled and the poor quarter is boiling seaweed.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.2.share: Buy a sack for the lane
paradise_isle.ev.famine.2.share.note: You buy rice on credit and eat seaweed yourself for a month.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.2.close.note: Your family is fed, and you avoid the poor quarter.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.3.text: The reef's fish have gone and the divers come back light.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.3.share: Teach the young to dive deep
paradise_isle.ev.famine.3.share.note: You teach them the blue-cave breath, and they bring home fish for all.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.3.close.note: You carry home fish while the shallows starve the others.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.4.text: The great school is late this year and the whole island watches the jetty for a sign.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.4.share: Share the last of the salt fish
paradise_isle.ev.famine.4.share.note: The salt fish stretches further than you feared, and the school arrives in time.
paradise_isle.ev.famine.4.close.note: The school comes, and the village remembers who hoarded through the lean weeks.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.1.text: The old custom: on the storm's anniversary each family keeps a lamp burning and speaks no name of the drowned.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.1.keep.note: You sit in the lamplight and keep the names unspoken.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.1.break.note: You speak your grandfather's name, and the room goes still, and his widow weeps with relief.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.2.text: Before the first sale of the season the market throws a fish back to the sea, for luck.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.2.keep.note: The season is good, and the old ones nod at you.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.2.break.note: You pocket the coin, the old ones notice, and the season is only fair.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.3.text: The divers leave the first pearl of the season in the reef's blue cave, for the sea's favour.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.3.keep.note: The reef keeps its favour and your dives are lucky.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.3.break.note: You sell it well; a week later your line snaps on the biggest fish of the year.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.4.text: At a wedding, custom says the bride's boat must be rowed out and back by the groom's kin alone.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.4.keep.note: The rowing takes all afternoon and the laughter carries across the water.
paradise_isle.ev.tradition.4.break.note: The boat comes back fast; the grandmother's face says what no one will.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.1.text: The keeper is retiring and must choose who will tend the lamp after him.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.1.write.note: You learn the vigil and the keeper sleeps easy at last.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.1.silent.note: Another takes the lamp, and you keep your nights free.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.2.text: The market master would teach his ledgers to one young islander.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.2.write.note: You learn to read the tide of prices, and the market's future opens to you.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.2.silent.note: You keep your hands wet and your head clear, and someone else balances the scales.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.3.text: An old diver wants to pass on the blue-cave breath before his lungs give out.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.3.write.note: You take the breath and the old man's stories, and he dies content.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.3.silent.note: The trick dies with him, and the blue cave keeps its secret.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.4.text: Your craft—net, boat, or song—should be passed on, but the young are leaving for the mainland.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.4.write.note: The apprentice is clumsy and then good, and the craft outlives you.
paradise_isle.ev.legacy.4.silent.note: The loom, or the last song, is packed away and never replaced.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.1.text: A trader offers good coin for a night's work that wants no questions asked.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.1.resist.not: You refuse, the trader finds another boat, and your sleep is clean.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.1.yield.note: The work is heavy and the coin is real, and you do not ask where it came from.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.2.text: A neighbour's wife makes you an invitation that no one else must know of.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.2.resist.not: You row out early and stay out till dark, and the moment passes.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.2.yield.note: The village has long eyes, and the secret is not a secret for long.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.3.text: A diver says there is a cave of pure pearl-shell that the Elders have forbidden to touch.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.3.resist.not: You dive elsewhere and leave the cave's wealth to the sea.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.3.yield.note: One shell is enough to change your year, and you think of it every dive after.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.4.text: Alone at the Lookout you see a boat in trouble, and no one to say whether you acted.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.4.resist.not: You take your boat into the swell and pull two strangers from the water.
paradise_isle.ev.temptation.4.yield.note: The sea takes them; no one ever knows, and you do.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.1.text: A boat is caught in the rip below the lighthouse and its crew is shouting.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.1.help.note: You pull two men aboard and your own boat nearly swamps.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.1.pass.note: The other boats reach them; one man does not come back.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.2.text: A child has slipped off the market steps into deep water.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.2.help.note: You pull the child up coughing and the market cheers your name.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.2.pass.note: The rope reaches; the child is safe, and you stay dry.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.3.text: A young diver's line is caught and he cannot surface.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.3.help.note: You dive with your knife and bring him up blue-lipped and living.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.3.pass.note: His brother cuts him free, and is the one he thanks.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.4.text: A stranger, ill-dressed for the water, is swept off the pier by a wave.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.4.help.note: You haul him onto the pilings and he gasps your name before he knows it.
paradise_isle.ev.rescue.4.pass.note: You come back with the boat; the pier is empty and the sea is calm.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.1.text: The chapel offers to buy your family's catch at a good price, if you will lend your voice to the singing each festival.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.1.deal.note: You sing each festival, badly at first, and the market remembers your face kindly.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.1.walk.note: You keep the price and your silence, and the chapel buys from another.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.2.text: The market master offers you the best stall for a cut of everything you sell.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.2.deal.note: The best stall pays for itself twice over.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.2.walk.note: You keep every coin of a smaller trade, and your back aches for it.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.3.text: A mainland boat offers to buy your whole pearl-shell harvest, sight unseen, at a fair price.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.3.deal.note: The coin is good and the boat sails; the shell was worth more, you later hear.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.3.walk.note: The price rises and you sell well, or the shell sits and dulls.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.4.text: A stranger on the pier will trade a fine foreign fishing rod for your old net.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.4.deal.note: The rod casts farther than you dreamed, and the old net drifts out with the tide.
paradise_isle.ev.bargain.4.walk.note: You keep the net your grandmother wove, and think of the rod at odd moments.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.1.text: The typhoon is coming and the boats of Shell Bay are still on the sand.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.1.shelter.n: You haul three boats to high ground, including one that is not yours.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.1.self.note: You bring your boat in and watch the others break on the sand.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.2.text: The wind takes a roof off and an old woman is trapped under the beams.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.2.shelter.n: You lift the beams with two others and she lives, and your hands are torn.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.2.self.note: Your family is safe and dry, and you hear the old woman cry until the wind drowns her.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.3.text: The storm surge is pushing a boat onto the reef where it will break apart.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.3.shelter.n: You wade chest-deep and get a line to the boat, and it holds.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.3.self.note: The boat breaks on the reef; the crew swims in, and no one blames you, quite.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.4.text: The storm takes the lookout's shutters and the keeper cannot hold them alone.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.4.shelter.n: You lash the shutters with wet rope, and the lamp stays lit all night.
paradise_isle.ev.storm_night.4.self.note: The lamp goes out, and a boat in the dark finds the shore by luck.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.1.text: The keeper will teach the stars to anyone who climbs the tower before dawn.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.1.study.not: You learn the southern stars and can fix your position by them.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.1.play.note: You keep your rest and stay lost when the fog comes.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.2.text: The market master offers to teach you the reading of weather signs.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.2.study.not: You learn to smell a squall coming, and the boats heed your word.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.2.play.note: Your instincts are good until the day they are wrong.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.3.text: An old diver will teach the names of every fish on the reef, if you have the patience.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.3.study.not: You learn the reef as a language and can call the fish by name.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.3.play.note: You fish well and know less than you might.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.4.text: A retired singer offers to teach you the old tide-songs before her voice goes.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.4.study.not: You learn the songs, and the songs keep the fleet together in fog.
paradise_isle.ev.scholarship.4.play.note: The old songs fade, and one by one the boats forget their rows.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.1.text: The chapel would name you Keeper of the Nets, to sit with the Elders.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.1.accept.note: You sit with the Elders and learn how heavy a small island's word can be.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.1.decline.note: You keep your boat and your mornings, and the Elders choose another.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.2.text: The market would raise a carved figurehead at your stall for the best catch of the year.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.2.accept.note: Your figurehead watches the market all season, and the young envy you.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.2.decline.note: You ask that the honour go to the youngest fisher instead.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.3.text: The island would name the new boat after your family.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.3.accept.note: Every launching of that boat is a small festival, and your mother cries.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.3.decline: Name it for the old ones
paradise_isle.ev.honor.3.decline.note: You name it for the drowned instead, and the old ones weep and are glad.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.4.text: The watch would give you the honour of lighting the festival fire.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.4.accept.note: You light the fire, the whole island cheers, and your hands shake.
paradise_isle.ev.honor.4.decline.note: A child lights the fire and remembers it all their life.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.1.text: Your best knife, your grandfather's, is gone somewhere between the boat and the house.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.1.call.note: You find it in the wet sand at the tide line, rust already at the edge.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.1.wait: Wait, and it will turn up
paradise_isle.ev.lost.1.wait.note: It turns up a month later in a neighbour's shed, and neither of you says a word.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.2.text: A storm has scattered the village's drying nets down the beach and into the sea.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.2.call.note: The village combs the beach together and finds most of the nets.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.2.wait.note: You mend your own and let the rest go; the season is thinner for it.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.3.text: Your boat has slipped its mooring in the night and drifted out toward the reef.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.3.call: Take the other boat and search
paradise_isle.ev.lost.3.call.note: You find her on the reef's edge, unhurt, bailed and towed home.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.3.wait.note: The tide brings her back, scraped, and you spend a week caulking her.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.4.text: A child is missing since the market closed, and the light is going.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.4.call.note: You raise the island; the child is found asleep under a boat, and the mother cannot stop shaking.
paradise_isle.ev.lost.4.wait.note: You find the child where you looked first, and wish you had raised the island sooner.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.1.text: You dream the lamp goes dark and a ship comes onto the rocks, and you wake with salt on your lips.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.1.follow.note: You find the wick trimmed too short and set it right; the dream does not return.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.1.wake.note: You sleep again, and the next week a boat does come close, and does not strike.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.2.text: In a dream your grandmother shows you a shoal of fish in a place you have never fished.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.2.follow.note: The shoal is there, and the catch feeds the village through a lean month.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.2.wake.note: You forget the place by noon, and the lean month is lean.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.3.text: You dream of a voice under the reef calling a name that might be yours.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.3.follow.note: You find only a hollow in the coral where the current sings, and you are calmer after.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.3.wake.note: You shake off the dream, and it comes back for three nights.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.4.text: You dream your drowned friend walks the pier and tells you where he left his boat.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.4.follow.note: The boat is there as he said, and you bring it home to his widow.
paradise_isle.ev.dream.4.wake.note: You wake and say his name aloud, and the pier is empty and the moon is high.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.1.text: At the festival a fisherman bets you cannot swim the bay's width and back before the tide turns.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.1.match.note: You make the far shore with your lungs burning and the crowd counting.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.1.fold.note: You decline, and he calls you wise, or coward, depending on who tells it.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.2.text: The market bets on whose boat will land the first fish of the season.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.2.match.note: Your line goes taut first, and the market pays you twice.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.2.fold.note: The other boat wins, and you keep your coin and your calm.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.3.text: A diver bets he can reach the blue cave floor and back; the stake is a season's catch.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.3.match.note: He surfaces pale and shaking, just short, and pays you.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.3.fold.note: You refuse to bet on a man's lungs, and he dives anyway, and lives.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.4.text: The watch bets you cannot name the night's weather by the smell of the wind.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.4.match.note: You name a squall, and the squall comes by midnight, and the watch buys the drinks.
paradise_isle.ev.bet.4.fold.note: You shrug and the sky does as it likes, and the watch is impressed by neither.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.1.text: An old woman lives alone in a cave at the end of Shell Bay and knows every herb on the island.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.1.learn.note: She teaches you which leaf stops a fever, and you use it for years.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.1.mock.note: She hears you, and the herbs she would have taught you stay in the cave.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.2.text: A silent man mends shoes in a shed behind the village and never comes to the festivals.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.2.learn.note: He tells you, once, about the wife he lost to the sea, and you understand his silence.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.2.mock.note: You leave him be, and years later learn he was a singer before the grief.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.3.text: A diver lives on the far side of the reef and dives alone, and no one knows his name.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.3.learn.note: He teaches you the blue cave and the patience to wait for the fish.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.3.mock.note: You keep your distance, and the far reef keeps its secrets.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.4.text: An old sailor sits at the pier's end all day, watching the horizon for a ship that will not come.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.4.learn.note: He tells you of the wreck and the ship that left without him, and you sit till dark.
paradise_isle.ev.hermit.4.mock.note: You think him mad, and he is; the ship comes in one evening, and it is a funeral.
paradise_isle.ev.quiet.text: The sea is flat and the day is long; you mend your nets and let the hours pass.
paradise_isle.ev.omen.text: A white bird lands on your mast and stays; the old ones say it is a good sign, and you hope they are right.
paradise_isle.ev.hard.text: The fish are shy today and every knot you tie slips.
paradise_isle.ev.dread.text: A cold current moves under the bay and something in you will not settle.
paradise_isle.ev.bounty.text: A stranger overpays for a small fish and waves away the change.
paradise_isle.ev.weariness.text: Your arms are heavy from the oars and your thoughts keep drifting to shore.
paradise_isle.beh.care.1: Bathes your cuts in salt water
paradise_isle.beh.care.1.res: The sting of the salt cleaned your wounds.
paradise_isle.beh.care.2: Mashes a herb poultice onto your leg
paradise_isle.beh.care.2.res: A bitter green leaf drew the fever out.
paradise_isle.beh.care.3: Sits with you through the night watch
paradise_isle.beh.care.3.res: Someone kept the lamp lit while you slept.
paradise_isle.beh.meal.1: Brings a bowl of fish stew
paradise_isle.beh.meal.1.res: The stew was hot and thick with the morning's catch.
paradise_isle.beh.meal.2: Leaves a basket of mangoes at your door
paradise_isle.beh.meal.2.res: You tasted the sweetness of the season.
paradise_isle.beh.meal.3: Calls you to the family table
paradise_isle.beh.meal.3.res: You ate with others, and ate better for it.
paradise_isle.beh.coin.1: Slips a few coins into your palm
paradise_isle.beh.coin.1.res: Your purse grew heavier by a little.
paradise_isle.beh.coin.2: Pays the fishmonger what you owe
paradise_isle.beh.coin.2.res: An old market debt was settled for you.
paradise_isle.beh.coin.3: Lends you a pouch of pearl-money
paradise_isle.beh.coin.3.res: A pouch of coin eased your trouble.
paradise_isle.beh.talk.1: Shares the day's gossip at the well
paradise_isle.beh.talk.2: Argues tides and weather with you
paradise_isle.beh.talk.2.res: The argument left your head clearer.
paradise_isle.beh.talk.3.res: After the long talk you were less alone.
paradise_isle.beh.teach.1: Shows you how to mend a net's eye
paradise_isle.beh.teach.1.res: You learned a knot that holds.
paradise_isle.beh.teach.2: Teaches you to read the clouds
paradise_isle.beh.teach.2.res: You can smell a squall before it comes.
paradise_isle.beh.teach.3.res: You kept a song that keeps the fleet together.
paradise_isle.beh.train.1.res: Your arms and lungs grew stronger.
paradise_isle.beh.train.2: Hauls nets beside you till dark
paradise_isle.beh.train.2.res: You found a new strength in your back.
paradise_isle.beh.train.3: Teaches you the diver's slow breath
paradise_isle.beh.train.3.res: You learned to go deeper on one breath.
paradise_isle.beh.warn.1: Warns you off the reef at low tide
paradise_isle.beh.warn.1.res: You kept clear of the shoal in time.
paradise_isle.beh.warn.2: Warns you the tide will turn early
paradise_isle.beh.warn.2.res: You brought the boat in before the current.
paradise_isle.beh.warn.3: Warns you of a mainland trader's tricks
paradise_isle.beh.warn.3.res: You kept your coin and your trust.
paradise_isle.beh.gift.1: Gives you a net of this morning's snapper
paradise_isle.beh.gift.1.res: You received a net full of silver fish.
paradise_isle.beh.gift.2.res: A shell the colour of dawn warmed your palm.
paradise_isle.beh.gift.3: Gives you a string of old pearl
paradise_isle.beh.gift.3.res: An heirloom pearl went around your neck.
paradise_isle.beh.song.1: Hums the tide-song while you work
paradise_isle.beh.song.1.res: The song made the work lighter.
paradise_isle.beh.song.2: Sings the song of the drowned sailors
paradise_isle.beh.song.2.res: The old song carried you a long way out.
paradise_isle.beh.song.3: Sings a wedding song at your door
paradise_isle.beh.song.3.res: The wedding song stirred something tender.
paradise_isle.beh.rest.1: Spreads a mat in the shade for you
paradise_isle.beh.rest.1.res: A nap in the shade gave you back an hour.
paradise_isle.beh.rest.2: Takes the oars so you can sleep
paradise_isle.beh.rest.2.res: You slept while the boat found her own way.
paradise_isle.beh.rest.3: Keeps the fire low and watches over you
paradise_isle.beh.debt.1: Borrows a few coins and repays them
paradise_isle.beh.debt.1.res: Your purse was lighter for a while.
paradise_isle.beh.debt.2: Asks you to cover a market debt
paradise_isle.beh.debt.2.res: You paid an old debt for someone.
paradise_isle.beh.debt.3: Begs a large loan for a boat
paradise_isle.beh.debt.3.res: A great sum went out and has not come back.
paradise_isle.beh.rumor.1: Whispers a rumour about your family
paradise_isle.beh.rumor.2: Tells the market your catch was poached
paradise_isle.beh.rumor.2.res: Someone belittled your work behind you.
paradise_isle.beh.rumor.3: Spreads a wild tale about you
paradise_isle.beh.taunt.1: Mocks your knots to your face
paradise_isle.beh.taunt.1.res: The jeer stung sharper than it should.
paradise_isle.beh.taunt.3: Calls you a coward before the market
paradise_isle.beh.scheme.1: Steals your stall at the market
paradise_isle.beh.scheme.2: Cuts the net you set overnight
paradise_isle.beh.scheme.2.res: A night's work was cut to shreds.
paradise_isle.beh.scheme.3: Complains about you to the Elders
paradise_isle.beh.scheme.3.res: A complaint reached the Elders' bench.
paradise_isle.beh.upkeep.1: Mends your nets while you rest
paradise_isle.beh.upkeep.1.res: Your nets were set in order.
paradise_isle.beh.upkeep.2: Keeps your boat bailed and tidy
paradise_isle.beh.upkeep.2.res: Your boat was bailed and ready.
paradise_isle.beh.upkeep.3: Speaks for you at the council
paradise_isle.beh.upkeep.3.res: A good word was said in your name.
paradise_isle.off.visit.1: Invites you to a family supper
paradise_isle.off.visit.1.text: Nan asks you to the family table, saying the pot is too big for one.
paradise_isle.off.visit.1.yes.res: The supper was loud and warm and you stayed late.
paradise_isle.off.visit.1.no.res: The pot was big and the table was quiet.
paradise_isle.off.visit.2.text: A cousin is marrying at the Palm Shore and wants you to row the bride's boat.
paradise_isle.off.visit.2.yes.res: You rowed the bride across and the whole shore cheered.
paradise_isle.off.visit.2.no.res: Another took the oars, and your family noticed.
paradise_isle.off.favor.1: Asks you to mind the boat
paradise_isle.off.favor.1.text: A neighbour asks you to watch his boat while he carries his sick wife to the chapel.
paradise_isle.off.favor.1.yes.res: You bailed and watched till he came back, and he did not forget it.
paradise_isle.off.favor.1.no.res: He found another hand, and something between you cooled.
paradise_isle.off.favor.2.text: A fisher asks you to vouch for him to the market master for a season's credit.
paradise_isle.off.favor.2.yes.res: He paid his credit in full, and the market trusted your name.
paradise_isle.off.favor.2.no.res: He took the refusal quietly, and never asked again.
paradise_isle.off.venture.1: Offers a share in the pearl dive
paradise_isle.off.venture.1.text: A diver offers you a share of a pearl haul if you supply the boat.
paradise_isle.off.venture.1.no: Keep the boat out of it
paradise_isle.off.venture.1.yes.res: The haul was good; your share bought new sails.
paradise_isle.off.venture.1.no.res: The dive went ahead, and the boat stayed yours and idle.
paradise_isle.off.venture.2: Offers a share in a trading run
paradise_isle.off.venture.2.text: The Boatwright wants a partner for a run of salted fish to the next bay.
paradise_isle.off.venture.2.yes.res: The run turned a profit and the partnership held.
paradise_isle.off.venture.2.no.res: You kept your coin, and watched the profit sail off without you.
paradise_isle.off.feast.1.text: The market calls the catch-feast and every hand is welcome at the long table.
paradise_isle.off.feast.1.yes.res: You ate till you could not move and told the best lie of the year.
paradise_isle.off.feast.1.no.res: You mended nets while the market sang, and the quiet was almost enough.
paradise_isle.off.feast.2: Calls you to the wedding feast
paradise_isle.off.feast.2.text: The Boatwright's daughter is married at moonrise and the whole island is called.
paradise_isle.off.feast.2.yes.res: You danced till your feet ached and lost your voice in the singing.
paradise_isle.off.feast.2.no.res: You tended the coals and heard the music from the edge, and were glad.
paradise_isle.off.secret.1: Offers to tell you a secret
paradise_isle.off.secret.1.text: A friend wants to tell you a thing about the Elders that must go no further.
paradise_isle.off.secret.1.yes.res: You learned something you cannot unknow about the common land.
paradise_isle.off.secret.1.no.res: You kept your peace, and the secret passed you by.
paradise_isle.off.secret.2: Offers to trust you with a secret
paradise_isle.off.secret.2.text: A diver wants to entrust you the location of a hidden reef, on his life.
paradise_isle.off.secret.2.yes.res: You keep the reef's name in your mouth and never spend it.
paradise_isle.off.secret.2.no.res: The secret went with him to the deep, and you wonder.
paradise_isle.off.duel.1.text: A rival fisher challenges you to gut a hundred fish before the noon bell.
paradise_isle.off.duel.1.yes.res: Your hands were a blur and the market cheered.
paradise_isle.off.duel.1.no.res: He crowed, and you kept your hands clean.
paradise_isle.off.duel.2.text: A young crew bets their new hull against yours in the festival race.
paradise_isle.off.duel.2.yes.res: You beat them by a length and earned their respect.
paradise_isle.off.duel.2.no.res: They raced anyway, lost to another boat, and called you wise.
paradise_isle.off.trade.1: Offers to trade fish for fruit
paradise_isle.off.trade.1.text: A neighbour offers breadfruit for your snapper, straight across.
paradise_isle.off.trade.1.yes.res: Both tables were better for it.
paradise_isle.off.trade.1.no.res: Your family ate fish and wanted for nothing else.
paradise_isle.off.trade.2: Offers a boat for your net
paradise_isle.off.trade.2.text: The Boatwright will trade a small dinghy for the net your grandmother wove.
paradise_isle.off.trade.2.yes.res: The dinghy is nimble, and you swear you can still feel the old net's knots.
paradise_isle.off.trade.2.no.res: You kept the net, and the dinghy went to another.
paradise_isle.off.journey.1: Asks you along to the far reef
paradise_isle.off.journey.1.text: A diver is sailing for the far reef and asks for a second pair of hands.
paradise_isle.off.journey.1.yes.res: The far reef was strange and rich and nearly took you.
paradise_isle.off.journey.1.no.res: You stayed, and heard his stories secondhand.
paradise_isle.off.journey.2: Asks you to crew the mainland run
paradise_isle.off.journey.2.text: The Boatwright wants you to crew a run to the mainland port.
paradise_isle.off.journey.2.yes.res: You saw a mainland quay and were glad to come home.
paradise_isle.off.journey.2.no.res: The run went well and you kept your feet on island stone.
paradise_isle.plugin.desc: Extra neighbourly behaviours and hidden island scores for Paradise Isle.
